brief: A sturdy step for my toddler to stand on so they can reach the bathroom sink.

requirements.evidence: 4x full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full) joined in one body at level 0 with 4 top covers, open faces capped, lockJoints applied; low 80mm single-storey platform ~310x393mm deck (trainers prop on deck f5 shows standing use); check_build meshClash clear, no errors
requirements.requirement: Low step platform a toddler can stand on

requirements.evidence: Single-storey 80mm boost on wide stable footprint; deck of 4 covers staged with trainers to show standing use. Actual sink-reach depends on child height and sink height, which the configurator does not model.
requirements.requirement: Raises child to reach bathroom sink

requirements.evidence: Wide 4-cell footprint resists tipping and joints are bolted (jointBolt x5); but parts are 3D-printed in a user-chosen material and the configurator checks fit/collisions only, with no load rating, slip, strength or stability testing
requirements.requirement: Sturdy and safe under a toddler's weight

finish.summary: Built a low, wide single-step platform (4 full bases, covered, capped, joints locked) giving an 80mm boost for a toddler at the sink; staged with shoes and verified clear. Strength/slip/load safety cannot be verified in the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
